name: Inclined Twin-Roller Elevator
rationale: Powered wheels above an inclined channel guide would draw objects from a low entry and advance them upward. Compliant intake wheels and a chain-linked upper roller concept provide continuous feeding rather than lifting a fixed cradle.
scoring_sequence: Contact objects with the lower rollers.
Feed them up the inclined guide.
Reverse or advance to release near the target.
hypothesis: A staged roller path may move objects upward without a separate lift, but compression, traction, guide clearance, feed timing, and discharge direction are unknown.
unresolved_connections: Roller shafts, bearing locations, collars, screw stacks, motor-to-sprocket coupling, chain length/tension, inclined-frame bracing, and chassis attachment are not mating-solved; most transmission CAD is absent.
The compiler pose does not establish wheel compression against the object, clearance through the channel, or synchronization between rollers.
Side guides, an entry funnel, an anti-rollback feature, and discharge retention are missing, so jamming or unintended ejection is possible.
The 31-degree guide and 101.6 mm spacing have not been calibrated to benchmark objects or field-goal openings.
